items.title: Joanne Brackeen interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 10, 2001
items.q: I highly regard him and respect him. ... my students use so many of his transcriptions

ctx.x: Oh yeah. Of course, yes. © Fillius Jazz Archive -10-

I had a couple of things people have said about you. And Bill Dobbins at Eastman, he said your, “Approach to playing is unique especially in regards to rhythmic development.” Does that strike you as a good statement do you think?

I guess so. I mean that’s me. I would have to agree that he’s certainly — my students use so many of his transcriptions in learning things and learning how to play. There are some key things that he’s done, been a transcriber of, so he does a close study of people and things. So I highly regard him and respect him.
